title: A recap of the worked example
statement: In independent practice, let students open a recap of what the worked example did at each step, drawn from the example's own material rather than the current answer.
detail: A version-3 inference lesson design for a Grade 3 course gives every independent step a collapsible recap of what was done in the modelled step, which refers back to the worked example on an earlier section of the story, plus contextual help (`downloads/5. Curriculum/Instruction/3.1 - Fantasy Classics - Lesson Designs/3.1 - 2. Aladdin and the Wonderful Lamp, Part 2 (FICTION, INFER) — v3 (new INFER design).docx`, lines 6 and 213 of its text). The first step's recap describes the process the model followed, reading the question and seeing that the story never says why, with no answer for the new section (line 217). No outcome was measured.
against: A later run found: a repair in a Grade 3 reading course replaced carryover recaps of the worked example with summaries of the current task's own material, after a scan warned that an unsignposted recap about another character can be taken for a hint about the learner's own question (`grade3-reading/artifacts/qc-2026-09-29-staging/ADJUDICATION-pr662.md`). A later run found: A later ruling in a Grade 3 reading course bars hints that recap a past screen: a hint must coach the current screen, since one that re-narrates an earlier step or model action teaches the child to listen for the wrong screen, and all 16 recap strings were rewritten as present-tense coaching for the current step (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/g3-reading/iteration-6/distilled/04-CONTENT-AUTHORING.md`). A later run found counter-evidence (`grade3-reading/artifacts/qc-2026-09-29-staging/ADJUDICATION-pr662.md`).

evidence.quote: every Independent (Phase 3) step now carries a toggleable … recap that references the cave model
Replaced carryover London/Lost Boys summaries with the current Neverland/Hook fit-word summaries.

A child who taps the hint mid-task, without holding the "watch me think" page in memory, will read "gloomy, miserable, strict" or "Lost Boys... gentle, lonely" while looking at a Neverland/Hook question and can easily mistake it for a hint about their OWN answer
A hint must always coach the CURRENT screen, never recap a past one.
Fixed by rewriting all 16 `teacher_recap` strings to present-tense current-step coaching
persistent 'What did Scout do?' button; Step 4 unskippable;

evidence.path: sources/Readventure - Lesson Design and Scaffolding - Updated.docx
evidence.quote: A persistent button, "What did Scout do?", reopens them at any point during Part 3, and a child can jump straight to one step rather than replaying the whole thing.
This is separate from the "I need help" button, which calls the refresher: this one is a reference, not a rescue, and it costs the child nothing on the pacing signal.
